en: Lake Lanao is the deepest lake in the Philippines, not Laguna de Bay, which is only the largest.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, while Mount Pulag is only the third highest peak.
The endangered tamaraw is found exclusively in the wild on the island of Mindoro, not the island of Mindanao.
Mayon Volcano has a perfect cone shape because it is a stratovolcano, not a broad, gently sloping shield volcano.
The Philippine Sea is located on the eastern side of the archipelago, directly facing the vast Pacific Ocean.
The Philippine tarsier is native to Bohol, Samar, Leyte, and Mindanao, not exclusively to the islands of the Visayas.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is located in the Sulu Sea, not the West Philippine Sea.
The Philippines experiences only two main seasons, the wet and dry seasons, rather than the four seasons found in temperate countries.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching about 505 kilometers, not the much shorter Pasig River.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is a distinct, separate region in Luzon, not a sub-region of the Ilocos Region.
The San Bernardino Strait separates the island of Luzon from the Visayas, not the Visayas from the island of Mindanao.
The Philippines actually consists of 7,641 islands, which is more than the previously taught number of 7,107 islands.
